security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel, when SBI ecalls pass kernel buffer addresses to M-mode firmware handlers, and those buffers cross PMP entry boundaries or are only partially covered by an unlocked (L=0) PMP entry, M-mode access faults despite the kernel's assumption that M-mode can unconditionally access any unlocked region. The PMP matching rules (partial match → fail) now explicitly apply to M-mode, meaning even a single PMP entry boundary crossing within a kernel buffer handed to M-mode causes an unrecoverable access fault in firmware context.
security_spec.summary: PMP partial-match access failures now explicitly apply to M-mode even for unlocked (L=0) regions, meaning kernel buffers passed to SBI firmware handlers must be fully contained within a single PMP entry or risk M-mode access faults and silent data corruption.

findings.finding: Passes stack-local hart_mask address to M-mode via ecall a0 register. If the kernel stack page straddles a PMP entry boundary, M-mode firmware attempting to read this hart_mask will take an unrecoverable PMP access fault. No alignment or boundary check exists.

Passes stack-local hart_mask address to M-mode for all v0.1 RFENCE operations (REMOTE_FENCE_I, REMOTE_SFENCE_VMA, REMOTE_SFENCE_VMA_ASID). Same PMP boundary-crossing risk as __sbi_send_ipi_v01. M-mode reads the hart_mask from kernel stack memory; if that stack page crosses an M-mode PMP entry boundary, M-mode access faults with no recovery path.

Has page-boundary truncation (line 604-605) to avoid crossing OS page boundaries, but uses PAGE_SIZE (4KB) rather than PMP entry granularity. RISC-V PMP granularity (G field) ranges from 4 bytes to 4KB. A 4KB-aligned buffer can still cross PMP entry boundaries at smaller granularities (e.g., NAPOT G=1 gives 8-byte granularity). The physical address base_addr is passed directly to M-mode for read access.

Identical partial mitigation as sbi_debug_console_write: truncates to PAGE_SIZE boundary (line 633-634) but PMP entry granularity can be much smaller (4 bytes minimum). M-mode writes to the kernel buffer at base_addr; if the buffer crosses a PMP entry boundary, M-mode write access faults.

Multi-page SBI NACL shared memory buffer (~10KB, spanning 3x 4KB pages). The kernel passes nacl->shmem_phys (base physical address) to M-mode via ecall. M-mode accesses the entire buffer for HFENCE operations. While alloc_pages() provides physically contiguous pages, the boundary between the buffer's first/last page and neighboring non-shared pages may cross a PMP entry boundary. Neither the kernel nor firmware validates PMP entry alignment.

SBI v0.2 RFENCE calls pass all data via registers (hmask, hbase, start, size, asid) with no kernel memory pointers. M-mode does not need to dereference any S-mode memory address from these ecalls. Compliant with respect to the PMP buffer boundary concern at the ecall interface.
findings.snippet:
case SBI_EXT_RFENCE_REMOTE_SFENCE_VMA:
	ret = sbi_ecall(ext, fid, hmask, hbase, start, size, 0, 0);

findings.finding: Enables the riscv_sbi_for_rfence static branch as a one-way gate. Once enabled, all TLB/cache maintenance operations route through SBI ecalls to M-mode without any runtime fallback. If M-mode encounters PMP access faults due to boundary crossings, there is no mechanism to revert to direct S-mode IPI-based shootdown (the on_each_cpu() path).
